title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, read from the neighbouring pages and partly inferred. G is GL_2 (or the group H) over a base S. σ is a section with Tr σ = 0 and det σ = −ν. By Cayley–Hamilton this gives σ² = ν, a scalar. σ is regular in Steinberg's sense, i.e. not a scalar multiple of the identity. T_σ is its centralizer, a 1-dimensional commutative group scheme (a torus when 2ν is invertible). N_σ is the normalizer: the τ for which τστ^{-1} stays in the line Γσ ⊕ scalars, i.e. τ(σ) = aσ + b. N'_σ ⊂ N_σ is the subgroup with τστ^{-1} = εσ, ε ∈ μ_2. The previous page gives the exact sequence 1 → T_σ → N'_σ → μ_2 → 1.

This page compares N'_σ with N_σ. Write τ(σ) = aσ + b with a ∈ Γ(G_m) and b ∈ Γ(O_S). Taking traces, and using Tr τ(σ) = Tr σ = 0, gives Tr(b·1) = 2b = 0.

If 2 is invertible, then b = 0. So τ(σ) = aσ, and comparing determinants (or squaring, since σ² = ν) gives a² = 1, so a ∈ μ_2. Hence (24): N'_σ = N_σ when all residue characteristics are ≠ 2. More generally the same argument works whenever 2 is a non-zero-divisor in Γ(S, O_S).

In characteristic 2 this fails. σ' = aσ + b satisfies Tr σ' = 0 and det σ' = det σ, so it is locally conjugate to σ. Since det(aσ + b) = a² det σ + ab Tr σ + b², the conditions read −νa² + b² = −ν together with 2b = 0. The second condition is automatic in characteristic 2, and the pair does not force b = 0. Example: ν = 1, b = 1 + a, since (a + b)² = 1.

The page then starts on the product group B'_0 × A_ρ × N'_σ. The next page shows it is isomorphic to the scheme G*_{ρ,σ} parametrizing solutions (α, β, μ, ε) of a twisted-conjugacy ('loop equation') relation. The point of the present computation is that the μ_2-extension N'_σ, not the full normalizer, is the right factor; in residue characteristic ≠ 2 the two agree.
errors: The sentence 'toute section de N'_σ est en fait une section de N_σ' is trivial as written, since N'_σ ⊂ N_σ. The intended statement must be the converse: when 2 is a non-zero-divisor, every section of N_σ lies in N'_σ. This is a slip of the pen (or a transcription inversion).

When 2 is only a non-zero-divisor rather than invertible, the argument gives equality on sections over S (and over flat S-schemes) only. It does not give equality of the schemes N_σ and N'_σ, since the fibres in characteristic 2 still differ. Grothendieck's wording 'sections' is careful here, but the scheme-level statement (24) needs residue characteristics ≠ 2.

ideas.what: In characteristic ≠ 2, the normalizer of a traceless regular element of GL_2, taken modulo scalars, equals the subgroup acting by ±1; this gives an extension of μ_2 by the centralizer torus.
ideas.modern_name: Normalizer of a maximal torus in GL_2 / Weyl group μ_2 = Z/2
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Borel, Steinberg; SGA 3 for the group-scheme version)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (normalizers of tori, Weyl group schemes) for the general framework

ideas.what: Failure in characteristic 2: affine reparametrizations σ ↦ aσ + b with b ≠ 0 preserve trace and determinant.
ideas.modern_name: Bad behaviour of normalizers of regular centralizers in characteristic 2

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification within a long computation of the solution scheme of the 'loop equation' for GL_2-type data. The characteristic-2 remark is elementary and standard.
transcription_corrections: Read 'sur une base S telle que 2 soit section régulière (i.e. non diviseur de zéro) dans Γ(S,O_S)'. The inserted 'section régulière' replaces the crossed-out 'non diviseur'.
'a est dans ε' is probably 'a est dans μ_2' (or 'a = ε'), i.e. a² = 1.
'dis qu'il satisfait' should read 'dès qu'il satisfait'.
'que n'impliquent nécessairement b=0' should read 'qui n'impliquent pas nécessairement b=0'.
'A_g' in the last line should be 'A_ρ', matching the next page.
